cohort: The study included 276,220 pregnant women monitored at the Unified Health System (SUS) in the city of Sao Paulo, Brazil, between 2012 and 2020, who had an initial weight recorded before 13 weeks and up to 15 days before delivery, and a single pregnancy.
finding: A high proportion of pregnant women experienced inadequate gestational weight gain, which was significantly associated with initial BMI, type of birth, color/ethnicity, marital status, women's age, and antenatal care visits.
mod_finding: Gestational weight gain was found to be associated with the type of birth.
